correctness.rationale: Switching by the center-normalized sign vector multiplies the signed influence at each receiving vertex by its own switching sign. Zeros and ties are preserved, and legal ignitions correspond in both directions. On the positive star, center-first ignition produces a constant word. If a leaf burns first, the next spread colors the center from that single leaf; no other leaf can yet acquire a color at this same simultaneous spread. At most one of them can then be ignited before the next spread colors all remaining leaves. An exceptional leaf is realized by igniting another leaf first and the chosen leaf in the opposite color after the center burns. Thus there are exactly 2(n+1) distinct words, with the center sign and exceptional leaf recovering the word. Global negation reduces plurality to the maximum number of positive vertices, so the error count is the minimum distance of the switching vector to the positive-star code. For q negative leaves the two center choices cost max(0,q−1) and 1+max(0,n−q−1); grouping by q gives the signing polynomial. The distances at q=0,1 are zero and at q=n the distance is 1. On 2≤q≤n−1 the distance is min(q−1,n−q), whose maximizers are centered at (n+1)/2. Including q=n in the small tie cases gives q=2,3 for n=3 and q=2,3,4 for n=4; beyond them, the maximizing radius is floor((n−1)/2), with one central weight for odd n and two for even n. Binomial counting and the freely paired center signs give the claimed signing and full-code deep-hole counts.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker was not executed and does not explicitly assert the full deep-hole table. The proof checks all weights and is not an extrapolation from test sizes.
